core_principles: Brahman is the only reality; the world is an illusion (Maya).
Atman (individual soul) is identical to Brahman.
Ignorance (Avidya) causes the illusion of separateness.
philosophy_advaita.definition: Advaita Vedanta is a school of Hindu philosophy that teaches non-dualism, asserting that the individual self (Atman) and the ultimate reality (Brahman) are one and the same.
features: Radical non-dualism—asserts absolute unity of Atman and Brahman
Emphasizes direct experience over ritual or belief
Uses logic, scriptural study, and meditation for realization
Universal applicability—transcends caste, creed, and era
goals: Realize the unity of Atman and Brahman.

key_concepts.atman: The true self, beyond body and mind.
key_concepts.avidya: Ignorance that binds beings to Samsara.
key_concepts.brahman: The ultimate, infinite, and changeless reality.
key_concepts.maya: Illusion that creates the perception of multiplicity.

key_scriptural_references.quote_summary: The wise see the same Self in all beings.

philosophy_advaita.purpose: To reveal the non-dual nature of reality, dissolving the illusion of separateness and guiding seekers to realize their true Self as Brahman. Advaita aims to end suffering by removing ignorance (avidya) and awakening direct knowledge (jnana) of oneness.

relation_to_other_concepts.dharma: Ethical living supports clarity for realization.
relation_to_other_concepts.karma: Actions cannot grant liberation; only knowledge can.

philosophy_advaita.unique_insights: Advaita is unique in its uncompromising assertion of oneness: 'Brahman alone is real, the world is an appearance, and the individual self is not different from Brahman.' It teaches that liberation is not something to be attained, but the recognition of what already is. Advaita’s influence extends far beyond India, shaping modern philosophy, psychology, and spirituality worldwide.
